observations: Photo 0 and 2 show a used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly still partially attached to an engine, sitting outdoors in a yard full of similar used parts.
A small sticker reading '3Y69' is visible on the transmission casing in photos 0 and 2; this looks like an internal stock/part tag, not a readable brand or model number.
Photo 1 is a close-up of an electrical connector/sensor plug on the transmission housing, showing dirt and oxidation consistent with a used, outdoor-stored part.
A watermark 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' appears across all photos; this is the seller's business name/watermark, not proof the part is a Porsche component or of any specific brand.
Surfaces are dusty, oily, and weathered, with no visible engine running, no test bench, and no odometer or vehicle context shown.
Other partial engines/transmissions are visible in the background, confirming a scrapyard/spare-parts lot setting.

claims.claim: We also deal in all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business claim; no photo or document shown that verifies scope of inventory or legitimacy of the shop.

risks.risk: Transmission may not shift or function correctly (internal wear, slipping, fluid contamination) since it cannot be tested from photos alone.
risks.proof: A video of the transmission being bench-tested or installed and run through gears.

risks.risk: Exact vehicle make/model/engine compatibility is unclear without a readable part number or VIN tag.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the OEM part/VIN sticker or casting number stamped on the housing.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unidentified-fitment used transmission, lowering buyer confidence and resale value

risks.risk: Visible corrosion/oxidation on connectors (photo 1) could indicate electrical or sensor faults.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all connector pins and a continuity/sensor test result.

risks.risk: Mileage/age of the donor vehicle is unknown, affecting wear estimate.
risks.proof: Odometer photo or vehicle history document from the donor car.

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit photo of the OEM part number or VIN tag on the transmission casing.
Video of the transmission being tested (bench spin or installed run) showing gear engagement.
Close-up of all electrical connectors showing no corrosion damage.
Any paperwork or photo from the donor vehicle indicating mileage or model year.
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as a used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly, but with no verifiable model, fitment, or functional proof, it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, possibly non-working used part.
